title: Europe seeks to deter Russia after attempted attack in Leipzig
subhead: Hostile acts attributed to Moscow are multiplying across Europe. On September 3, Copenhagen accused Moscow of preparing 'sabotage actions' against Denmark's defense industry. However, European countries remain divided over how to respond.

Kyiv shootout between intelligence service members exposes rift within Ukraine's security apparatus
subhead: An armed clash broke out between agents from Ukraine's Security Service and a special unit of military intelligence on Wednesday, September 2, in the heart of the capital. The incident forced President Volodymyr Zelensky to order an investigation.

title: Germany's low gas reserves spark fears of a new crisis
subhead: German gas storage facilities are only 53% full, well below levels at the same point in recent years. Companies in the sector point out that the economics of storage have shifted. The situation is creating new dependencies, particularly on American liquefied natural gas (LNG).

title: 'The question of meaning is the first you must ask yourself, even before taking out your camera': Jean-François Leroy, director of Visa pour l'image, pens letter to young photojournalists
subhead: In a book to be published in September, the co-founder and head of the international photojournalism festival in Perpignan, who died on August 31, addresses a letter to young photojournalists, urging them to approach their subjects with a journalistic rather than an aesthetic eye, and to learn from their elders.

title: Writer Rebecca Solnit still has hope: 'When we show up, we can make the future'
subhead: Ahead of the midterm elections, Solnit calls for progressives to mobilize against Donald Trump in her latest book. She urges readers to reflect on the progress made over the past 70 years to understand the significance of feminist, social and environmental struggles.

subhead: Since late August, sirens have sounded in the Ukrainian capital at an unprecedented rate not seen since the beginning of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022. This new reality has upended routines the city's 3.7 million residents.

title: Israel's right, threatened with possible electoral defeat, fractures and radicalizes
subhead: Ahead of the October 27 elections, tensions are beginning to surface within the governing coalition, particularly between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir. From the right to the far right, political factions are hardening their rhetoric to rally supporters.

title: In southern Lebanon, complex Hezbollah disarmament and Israeli strikes leave residents desperate
subhead: The Lebanese Army has sought to deploy and residents have tried to return to their destroyed homes in the towns of Zawtar al-Gharbieh, Froun and Srifa, designated 'pilot zones' in July. Meanwhile, Israeli shelling continues nearby.
